summary: Saratoga County, NY: a wooden lookout on Ohmer Mountain was built in 1911 and closed in 1916; its steel replacement went up on Hadley Mountain. No source describes the Ohmer site today.

facts.design: Wooden fire lookout tower, built October 1911
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the mountain

events.note: Wooden fire lookout tower built by the Conservation Commission in October 1911
Lookout operations ended because satisfactory arrangements for operating and maintaining the station could not be made
Steel tower on Hadley Mountain replaced the Ohmer lookout (1917 per Wikipedia text; Hadley build dates differ by source: 1916, 1917, 1920)

evidence.supports: wooden fire lookout built on Ohmer Mountain in October 1911
evidence.quote: In October 1911, the Conservation Commission built a wood fire lookout tower on the mountain.

evidence.supports: lookout operations ceased in 1916 because maintenance arrangements could not be made
evidence.quote: The tower ceased fire lookout operations in 1916, as arrangements couldn't be made to continue to maintain it.

evidence.supports: steel tower built on Hadley Mountain in 1917 to replace the Ohmer tower
evidence.quote: In 1917, a steel fire lookout tower was constructed on Hadley Mountain to replace the wood tower on Ohmer Mountain.

evidence.supports: 1916 report: Ohmer station could not be operated; steel tower and new station planned on Hadley
evidence.quote: Satisfactory arrangements could not be made for the operation of Ohmer Mountain station in Saratoga county, and plans are being made to erect a steel tower and equip a new station on Hadley mountain.

evidence.supports: Ohmer Mountain listed in Saratoga County as a platform tower, gone
evidence.quote: Ohmer Mountain Saratoga 43.33723 -74.04892 Platform Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Hadley tower is a prefabricated Aermotor structure built in 1917 (Wikipedia text)
evidence.quote: The tower is a prefabricated structure built by the Aermotor Corporation in 1917.

evidence.supports: plaque dates the original Hadley wood tower to 1916 and the current steel tower to 1920
evidence.quote: The plaque states that the original wood tower was erected in 1916. The current steel tower was built in 1920.

evidence.supports: Hadley tower added to the National Register in 2001
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2001.

evidence.supports: Glens Falls Chronicle gives 1917 for the Hadley tower
evidence.quote: The Hadley Mountain fire tower was built in 1917

evidence.supports: hikers make a 1.8-mile trek to the Hadley fire tower; as many as 20,000 a year
evidence.quote: as many as 20,000 hikers per year make the 1.8-mile trek to the fire tower atop the mountain

evidence.supports: committee hires a summit steward each summer
evidence.quote: Every summer the Hadley Mountain Fire Tower Committee hires a Summit Steward

evidence.supports: Hadley Mountain tower is in Saratoga County
evidence.quote: located on Hadley Mountain at Hadley in Saratoga County

evidence.supports: plaque at the base of the trail to the tower (source of the 1916 and 1920 dates)
evidence.quote: There is a plaque at the base of the trail which leads to the fire tower

evidence.supports: summit steward hired each summer to assist and educate hikers
tower stands atop the mountain at the end of the 1.8-mile trek
evidence.quote: the fire tower atop the mountain

sources.title: Ohmer Mountain - Forest Lookouts (quoting the New York State Conservation Commission 6th Annual Report, 1916)
Hadley Mountain steward report by David Cederstrom

notes_for_editor: No source found describes the Ohmer Mountain site today. Hadley build year conflicts across sources (1916 original wood tower and 1920 current steel tower per the plaque as Wikipedia reports it; 1917 per Wikipedia text and the Chronicle); not reconciled and the story says so. The 1916 report is quoted via the Forest Lookouts site, not checked against the report itself. Record kind 'platform' vs Wikipedia's 'wood fire lookout tower'; not treated as an error. Hadley is a replacement on another mountain, not a moved structure, and its tower is a separate site. No access or visit data for the Ohmer site.
